What is the best meal you've ever had?

I'm a big sushi fan and so far the best I've had were at Ichimura and Nakazawa. Both are in New York and the experience was amazing. If anyone wants to take their sushi experience to the next level these two places are a must try.

The very best meal I have had was a prime rib from the Hereford House in Kansas City. The fixings weren't what made this spectacular. It was how it was cooked rare. It was how tender it it was and how it melted in your mouth. It was the au jus that filled the plate. For $50 a head, it was well fucking worth it.
I'm partial to vegan pho. It's a warm bowl of happiness.

I live in a small area outside DC known for it's Korean culture and immigrants. There is a place outside my apartment with only one tiny sign in all Korean that has the best damn Korean barbeque I have ever eaten!

I went to Quebec City years ago and at at a restaurant (now long gone, sadly) called "A La Table De Serge Bruere".

Each table was booked only once or maybe twice per night. Dinner took over 3 hours. It was a tasting menu but surprisingly affordable. Everything was intricately prepared and delicious.

The one thing I remember that really impressed me with their attention to preparation was the fish course. They had cut the fish into three strips and had braided them before they were cooked. It sounds silly but given how delicious everything was, it just took things to the next level for me at the time.
Most disappointing: the first meal after I fasted for 48 hours, I felt like crap. Best would be greasey food after a 15k.

Pad kea Mao from a little Thai restaurant that used to be a long john silvers in northern ky. I've eaten at a Michelin star, and many other high end places but I like this dish more than any other food I've ever eaten. It was that good!

There's a chipper not far from where I live. It has the most divine chicken fillet burger I have ever tasted. It's like feeding off a heavenly angel who was cooked in the oven of God. A sauce, not too bland, or too sweet. Just perfect. And a lettuce leaf, the nicest lettuce leaf you will ever see, it's aesthetic beauty only matched by the finger licking taste of what can only be described as the world's most unique piece of lettuce. For this is a lettuce with an aroma and flavour not typical of a leaf vegetable, no.

The bun is heated to perfection, it will warm not only your mouth, but also your soul. The chicken fillet cannot be aptly described with words. It has been known to make those who eat it too fast orgasm, an orgasm so extreme that no other orgasm can ever match it. We eat and we think we have consumed the burger, but in reality, the burger has consumed us.

Few years back... Well more than a few years I suppose. I was visiting family in Italy, and at this point in my stay we were staying in a hotel in... I assume that if you like Janis Joplin, you're familiar with Grace Slick, if not, she's a must-listen. I don't mean 80s crappy rock-pop like We Built This City but classic acid-influenced stuff with Jefferson Airplane, like White Rabbit or Somebody To Love... So yes, Grace Slick is my ... second favourite.

My favourite is Sandy Denny - a great 70s electric folk / folk-rock singer from the UK. I think that you actually might enjoy her work, as she gave a similar vibe to Janis, and, like Janis she had an extremely powerful voice. Some classic pieces to showcase her skills: Matty Groves, Knockin' On Heavens Door, and her own compositions like: John The Gun or Late November (solo with piano, live). Many don't know that, but she was the only outside singer to sing on a Led Zeppelin album - she's the second voice in The Battle of Evermore from VI/zoso. Robert plant actually called her the best of British female singers.
